title: Edge-origin token router and adaptive sampling controller
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce an edge-attached request-origin token and a centralized adaptive sampling controller to reduce observability ingestion cost while preserving high-fidelity traces for latency/error investigation. This work spans edge middleware, language SDK changes, and an ingestion-side controller that issues dynamic sampling decisions based on downstream pipeline pressure and observed error/latency signals.
background: Current tracing strategy records fixed-rate sampling in SDKs and middleware which either overrecords in low-traffic services or under-records during rare error spikes. Ingest pipeline backpressure leads to dropped spans with no graceful degradation strategy. We need a deterministic, low-entropy token at the edge that preserves request origin metadata and enables downstream controllers to make coarse-grained sampling decisions without losing ability to reconstruct critical traces.
goals: Design a compact Edge Origin Token (EOT) carried in header or binary carrier for gRPC that encodes minimal provenance: ingress node ID, ingress timestamp (millis), client-correlation-hash, and short bloom of known high-priority routes
Implement token population in edge proxies (ingress) and HTTP/gRPC middleware for non-proxy ingress paths
Add SDK hooks to prefer preserving the EOT when starting spans and to expose fast accessors for the token for exporters

Build an adaptive sampling controller service that subscribes to pipeline metrics (ingest queue depth, export success rate, error rate) and broadcasts sampling overrides as lightweight policies to SDKs and edge proxies
Ensure sampling controller can request "always-sample" for requests matching EOT-derived signals (e.g., rare client-correlation-hash or flagged route) during anomaly windows
Measure end-to-end improvement: lower stored span volume by >=40% in steady state while retaining >=95% fidelity for top-N error cases and end-to-end latency outliers
acceptance_criteria: EOT format v1 defined and documented in a spec doc (Confluence link in links) with field lengths and migration story
Edge proxy (ingress) populates EOT for 100% of external requests with fallback semantics when header is present
SDKs (JS, Python, Go) expose a read/write accessor for EOT and default exporters attach the token to span metadata
Adaptive sampling controller can turn on/off per-service sampling override and propagate policies within 5s of metric threshold crossing in staging
End-to-end test harness demonstrating sampling controller reducing spans persisted by >=40% on a representative workload while retaining >95% of error traces
No user-visible request latency increase >2ms P50 at ingress due to token generation or propagation in canary rollout
Backward compatibility: services that do not understand EOT continue to function and traces are reconstructable via correlation headers
implementation_notes: EOT must be base64url-safe compact binary <=48 bytes on wire; human-readable debug variant allowed via query param
Use HMAC-256 over ingress node ID + timestamp + nonce for tamper-evidence; store key in KMS with rotation plan
Edge implementation: Envoy filter for automatic EOT injection and validation; fallback http header X-RW-EOT for legacy paths
SDK change: lightweight middleware hook (startSpanWithContext) to include EOT with minimal allocation; avoid full trace context parsing when not necessary
Sampling controller: stateless policy engine backed by Redis pub/sub for low-latency policy broadcasts, metrics consumed from existing ingestion metrics stream
Policy format: JSON lines with service globs, route globs, percentage override, ttl_seconds. Keep policies small to minimize bandwidth to edge proxies/SDKs
api_changes: Introduce carrier header 'x-rw-eot' (base64url) and gRPC binary metadata key 'x-rw-eot-bin'
Expose SDK API: getEdgeOriginToken(): string | null and setEdgeOriginToken(token: string) for advanced use cases
Add sampling override endpoint in internal control plane: POST /v1/sampling/policies with JSON policy body
infra_changes: Deploy Envoy filter to all global ingress clusters behind a feature flag
Provision small Redis cluster for controller pub/sub in staging and production
Add RBAC entries for control-plane service to publish sampling policies
Increase ingest pipeline retention for short period to validate reconstruction after sampling changes
telemetry: Dashboards: Sampling Volume vs Persisted Spans, Error-trace Recall over time, Ingest Queue Depth correlated with policy events
Tracing: controller action traces should include EOT when available for end-to-end debug
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): Deploy Envoy filter with EOT injection disabled but validation enabled to observe existing headers
Phase 2 (canary): Enable EOT injection for 5% of traffic on a single region servicing test accounts; deploy SDK changes as opt-in via feature flag
Phase 3 (wide): Enable injection globally and activate adaptive sampling controller in passive mode (suggestions only), collect 2 weeks of telemetry
Phase 4 (active): Enable controller policy broadcasts with conservative thresholds and monitor retention and error recall; iterate policy rules
Fallback: controller can push policy 'sample=100' for services affected by regressions; feature-flag kill-switch on control plane
test_plan: Unit tests for EOT encoding/decoding and HMAC verification
Integration tests: Envoy filter <-> SDK path roundtrip simulation for HTTP and gRPC
Load test: measure P50/P99 latency impact at ingress with EOT enabled at 10k rps and 100k rps profiles
Chaos test: simulate ingest pipeline backpressure and verify controller reduces persisted spans without losing >5% of critical error traces
Canary observability runbook: checklist with pre/post metrics and rollback criteria
risks: Token format changes could break older SDKs; mitigate with versioned header and negotiation
HMAC key compromise could allow attackers to craft high-priority tokens; require KMS and limited lifetime tokens
Reactive sampling may hide signals if policies are too aggressive; include safety floor to always retain a small reservoir of traces per service
Increased complexity at edge may add small latency; need tight performance budget and benchmarking
